added.title: Senior Stormwater & Environmental Compliance Program Manager
added.description:
Position Summary

Environmental consulting firm seeking a Senior Stormwater & Environmental Compliance Program Manager
with 15+ years of experience
delivering complex stormwater, NPDES, and water quality compliance services. This role leads client programs, manages multidisciplinary project teams, and supports business development through exceptional technical execution and client relationships.

Responsibilities

Client Program Leadership — Serve as primary client contact for stormwater compliance programs, ensuring high‑quality deliverables and proactive communication.
Stormwater & NPDES Compliance — Manage MS4, Industrial General Permit, and watershed‑based compliance programs across diverse industries and public agencies.
Technical Project Delivery — Lead monitoring programs, watershed studies, BMP evaluations, toxicity investigations, and regulatory reporting.
Regulatory Strategy & Policy Support — Prepare technical comment letters, interpret regulatory changes, and advise clients on compliance strategies.
Team & Project Management — Oversee project budgets, schedules, staffing, and quality control for multiple concurrent projects.
Business Development Support — Significant contributor to proposals, scopes of work, client presentations, and strategic growth initiatives.
BMP Selection & Implementation — Provide technical guidance on BMP selection, installation, inspection, and performance optimization.
Training & Client Capacity Building — Deliver training for client staff, tenants, and facility operators on stormwater compliance requirements.
Mentoring —Mentor junior and mid-level staff in professional development and building job and client relation skills.
Represent —Write, speak, present, and represent the company in technical symposiums, industry groups and publications.

Requirements

BS in Environmental Engineering or Environmental Science
15+ years of experience in environmental consulting, stormwater compliance, or water quality program management.
Strong knowledge of MS4 permits, NPDES regulations, Industrial General Permit, TMDLs, and watershed management.
Proven ability to manage multiple clients and projects simultaneously.
Excellent communication skills and ability to lead multidisciplinary teams.
Demonstrated experience preparing technical reports and regulatory documentation.
Certifications such as CPSWQ, QSD/QSP, QISP/ToR
Experience supporting airports, ports, municipalities, industrial facilities, or regional water agencies.
Active participation in professional organizations such as CASQA, IEA, or similar groups.

The pay range for this California position is $170,000- $220,000 per year; however, base pay offered may be higher or lower depending on the job-related knowledge, skills, and experience of the candidate.

Benefits

NV5 offers a competitive compensation and benefits package including medical, dental, life insurance, PTO, 401(k) and professional development/advancement opportunities.

Competitive Salary
Medical, dental, and supplemental insurance
Employee Assistance Program
Company paid Life & AD&D
Company paid Disability
401K Plan
Paid Holidays
Paid Time Off

Company Overview

NV5 delivers technology-enabled engineering, consulting, and geospatial solutions that help clients plan, design, and optimize infrastructure, buildings, utilities, and environmental systems. We bring together technical expertise, data, and innovative thinking to create resilient, high-performance assets. As part of TiC Solutions, alongside Acuren, we share a purpose: to shape and strengthen the physical world.

Our work starts with our people. We invest in their growth and never compromise on safety. We work as one team
across disciplines and geographies, bringing diverse perspectives and a shared purpose to complex challenges.

At NV5, we take pride in high-quality work that creates lasting value for our clients. We challenge the status quo, continuously improve, and turn insight into smarter designs, plans, and solutions. Join us to contribute your expertise and collaborate with our teams to help shape the infrastructure and systems the world relies on.

added.title: Senior Air Quality Control Specialist
added.description:
Overview

At UES, we’re a team of more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, geologists, inspectors, technicians, and drillers united by a shared purpose—to make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. As a national leader in geotechnical engineering, environmental consulting, and materials testing and inspection, we collaborate on transformative projects across transportation, energy, water, healthcare, and more. Learn more about the benefits of joining Team UES and our core values at careers.teamues.com.

Position Overview

As a Senior Air Quality Control Specialist, you'll serve as a trusted technical leader at the forefront of environmental compliance and sustainability initiatives. In this high-impact role, you'll shape air quality strategies, drive regulatory excellence, and help ensure operational success while protecting the environment.

You'll lead complex air permitting and compliance efforts, provide expert guidance on emissions management, and partner with project teams and leadership to develop innovative solutions that reduce environmental impact. As a subject matter expert, you'll influence critical business decisions, build strong relationships with regulatory agencies, mentor emerging professionals, and help advance best practices across the organization.

This is an opportunity for an experienced professional who wants to combine technical expertise, leadership, and environmental stewardship while making a visible impact on large-scale projects and operations.

Responsibilities

Lead air quality compliance programs, ensuring adherence to federal, state, and local regulations, including the Clean Air Act.
Oversee and conduct advanced air quality monitoring, emissions testing, and air dispersion modeling as needed.
Manage air permit applications, renewals, modifications, and associated compliance documentation.
Analyze complex air emissions data to identify trends, potential violations, and opportunities for improvement.
Develop and implement corrective action plans for air quality issues or non-compliance events.
Serve as the primary contact for regulatory agencies during inspections, audits, and compliance discussions.
Prepare, review, and submit high-level technical reports, compliance filings, and environmental impact assessments.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to junior specialists and other staff involved in air quality monitoring.
Collaborate with engineering, operations, and maintenance teams to optimize air pollution control equipment and processes.
Stay informed of evolving environmental laws, industry best practices, and emerging technologies in air emissions control.
Lead or participate in internal environmental audits and risk assessments related to air quality.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemical engineering, or related field; Master’s degree preferred.
5–8 years of progressive experience in air quality compliance, emissions monitoring, or environmental engineering.
In-depth knowledge of Clean Air Act regulations, New Source Review (NSR), Title V permits, and emissions reporting requirements.
Proficiency with air dispersion modeling tools and emissions monitoring systems.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to mentor and train others.
Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, and technical writing skills.
Proven ability to interface effectively with regulatory agencies and industry stakeholders.
Valid driver’s license with acceptable driving record.

Preferred Qualifications

Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD)
New Source Review (NSR) permitting
Nevada permitting
Mining permitting
Proficiency with air dispersion modeling systems, e.g., AERMOD Lakes Environmental and BREEZE AERMOD

Travel Requirements

This position requires occasional domestic overnight travel, approximately 10% to 20% of the time, to support

business objectives and client engagements. Travel may be both scheduled and on short notice, depending on

project needs. Destinations typically include job sites, field locations, or regional offices, where work may be

conducted in outdoor or operational environments. Adherence to all company safety protocols and use of PPE is

required during travel and on-site work.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

This position operates in a hybrid work environment, requiring flexibility to work effectively from both a professional office and field work site setting.
On-Site Office Requirements:
Work is performed at a desk for extended periods using a computer, phone, and standard office equipment in a climate-controlled office environment.
Regular in-person communication with team members, clients, and stakeholders is required.
Physical demands may include sitting for long durations, occasional standing, walking, bending, and lifting of materials up to 15 pounds.

Physical Requirements:
Ability to bend, twist, reach, stoop, kneel, climb, and balance as needed during both lab and fieldwork.
Ability to communicate effectively in both verbal and written formats in varied environments, often while wearing PPE.
Ability to use sensory capabilities to see (including close and distant vision, color perception, depth perception, and focus) and smell for observation and safety purposes.
